html:
Maltese is the language of Malta, descended from the Arabic spoken there after the Arab conquest of 870, but written in the Latin alphabet. It is the only Semitic language that is an official language of the European Union.

Arab rule ended when the Normans of Sicily took the islands in 1091, but the people kept speaking their Arabic. Over the next centuries it took in a great many words from Sicilian, Italian and later English, while keeping its Arabic grammar and everyday words.

For centuries Italian was the language of the church, law and the educated. Maltese was written down in a standard form only in the 1920s and became an official language in 1934, beside English. The language shows how Malta sits between Europe and the Arab world, much like its history under the Knights and the British.
sum: Maltese is the language of Malta, descended from the Arabic spoken there after the Arab conquest of 870, but written in the Latin alphabet. It is the only Semitic language that is an official language of the European Union.
